punchline: The same sugarcane farmers scored about 9 to 10 IQ points lower before the harvest than after it.
thirty_sec: Mullainathan and Shafir tested the same sugarcane farmers in India a month before and a month after the harvest. When money was short the farmers did markedly worse on cognitive tests, a gap of about 9 to 10 IQ points. In a lab game, poor players who could borrow also did worse. The authors say scarcity pulls attention toward the pressing need.
